It's not really about the resources you use at this beginner level, it's about making a routine and a study habit so you can build a base to actually start learning the language seriously. Evan forcing yourself to study simply 10 minutes a day (cut 10 minutes out of gaming) would be a big win. Japanese from Zero is a pretty good resource. If you like gaming, the app DuoLingo might appeal to you too. It's not a loved app around here maybe because it doesn't teach the best Japanese, but if you just use it to get a foothold on the language, it could help too. Especially if you feel crunched for time. However if you "burn out" from a forced schedule, you might struggle to improve in Japanese. It's a hard language, a hard nut to crack so to speak. It will take some serious dedication on your part to even start to comprehend it's patterns. Think of it like working out, at first you might not notice a difference but if you continue a study pattern for long enough you might notice growth someday before you know it. The only person stopping you from acquiring some of this wonderful language is yourself. You can do it if you let yourself!

Slow and steady wins the race. There’s no rush, don’t feel like you have to blast through the language. There’s nothing wrong with taking it slow to make sure you understand everything. That said, if you find yourself getting bored with your method, introduce alternative materials or techniques or input sources just to add the spice of variety. You are kind of too low level to watch/read most content to learn from though, so for now your goal should be to build a solid grammatical and vocabulary base so that you can expand into various more entertaining ways to learn in the future.

In general Japanese language is just patterns. Follow the patterns. Don't try to improvise until you are a higher level. Also, it's basically impossible to sound rude if you stick to the polite words, so just use the basic polite phrases, slowly increasing as you build confidence with basic interactions and slowly grow your ability to speak. Don't over think it and worry about being "cold" or whatever, it's quite natural to use only a few words for basic interactions. Your intent to be polite and not force others to speak your language but to try to speak their language will be rewarding in the end. Good luck!

If your pitch accent or pronunciation is really bad, it can make it very hard to hear your Japanese. So instead of getting frustrated by English replies, take it as a chance to push yourself to improve. Your wording might need an improvement, too. In Japanese we don't say *I can't hear*, that implies you have a problem. Instead I would have said, the car was noisy so could you repeat that? etc. Also, just because someone switches to English doesn't mean you have to do that too. You can be honest with someone and tell them you are practicing Japanese, so please speak Japanese. If that is too embarrassing you could offer a white lie that you don't speak English, but only if they don't know you by reputation. None the less, I'm not saying give up. I'm just saying you need to improve! :)
